subject: Clarify DPA processing annex: PII minimization flow & subprocessors (follow-up)
messages:
From: Jen Silver <jen.silver@maplehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: MapleHealth Legal <legal@maplehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: DPA clarifications: PII flows, subprocessors, and export scenarios

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our legal and privacy teams are doing a quick pass on the DPA annex and have three areas they want clarity on before we sign:

1) PII classification and minimization: Can you send a simple diagram that shows where raw identifiers, pseudonymized tokens, and inference telemetry are stored and which Redwood components touch each tier? We need to show this to our privacy counsel.

2) Subprocessors: we need an up-to-date roster with the role each subprocessors performs (e.g., monitoring, backups, vector DB) and whether they have access to cleartext data or only encrypted blobs.

3) Cross-border transfers: we have EU-based users and need to understand any scenarios where data might transit or be persisted in non-EU regions, and what contractual/technical mitigations you propose.

Can you respond with the diagram and a short summary we can include in the annex by EOD Monday? Also, my legal team may propose a couple of redlines to the DPA annex — I can attach them after our review.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Jen
Privacy & Compliance, MapleHealth

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jen Silver <jen.silver@maplehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 11:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications: PII flows, subprocessors, and export scenarios

Jen —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary and attachments below; full answers and a proposed annex paragraph are in the shared Drive link (see related_links). Attachments: redwood-maple-dataflow-may2028.svg and subprocessors_roster_may2028.csv.

1) PII classification & minimization
- Raw identifiers (PII tier 1) are ingested at the API boundary and written to an encrypted input queue for model routing. Only a short-lived tokenization step (Redwood Tokenizer) derives a pseudonymized key; raw identifiers are not stored beyond the tokenization window except for transient logs retained for 72 hours for debugging (configurable via Dedicated/Private).
- Pseudonymized tokens (PII tier 2) are stored in our ephemeral KV cache for inference; TTLs are set by policy and default to 12 hours for hosted customers.
- Inference telemetry (anonymized usage metrics) is aggregated and stored separately for 90 days.

2) Subprocessors (high level)
- VectorDB Inc. — managed vector store (encrypted storage, no cleartext access).
- ObservabilityCo — telemetry pipeline (aggregated metrics only).
- CloudInfraProvider (GCP/US) — compute and persistent disk (data at rest encrypted; KMS-managed keys per customer for Dedicated/Private).
- BackupPartner — snapshot storage for Dedicated customers (snapshots are encrypted; access only via HSM-protected keys).

See subprocessors_roster_may2028.csv for full roles and access scopes. Short answer: only Tokenizer and the runtime components perform any cleartext processing. All other subprocessors operate on encrypted or pseudonymized artifacts.

3) Cross-border transfers
- Hosted: routing policy defaults to region nearest the customer; EU customers are offered EU-only hosting by default.
- Exceptions: in rare failover or capacity-burst scenarios, requests may route through US compute; these are covered by our standard transfer annex and fallbacks in the DPA. We can add a contractual limit and notifcation SLA for cross-border transient processing.

Next steps
- Ive uploaded a one-page diagram and the roster to the Drive.
- Marissa will drive follow-up on the KMS custody language and proposed DPA redlines.
- If acceptable, propose a 30-min follow-up on Monday to run through redlines.

Thanks,

Aditya Rao
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Tom Liu <tom.liu@maplehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jen Silver <jen.silver@maplehealth.com>, MapleHealth Legal <legal@maplehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications: PII flows, subprocessors, and export scenarios

Aditya,

Thanks for the quick response and the diagrams — reviewed with legal. A couple of clarifying asks and two redline items from our counsel:

- Can you confirm whether BackupPartner holds any long-lived decryption keys? Counsel is focused on custody.
- For tokenization: is the tokenizer deterministic (same identifier -> same token) or salted? We need to know for re-identification risks.
- Redline 1: explicitly enumerate subprocessors that may access logs containing identifiers (even transiently) and require notification within 48 hours prior to onboarding new subprocessors that could access identifiers.
- Redline 2: add an export exhibit that describes fallbacks (region-to-region routing) and the maximum duration an EU-origin request may be processed outside EU before being stopped/escorted to EU-only resources.

Quoted for context:
> On Fri, 11 May 2028 at 11:01 AM Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Short answer: only Tokenizer and the runtime components perform any cleartext processing.
> > All other subprocessors operate on encrypted or pseudonymized artifacts.

Wed appreciate Marissa or Jonas taking the lead on the KMS and export exhibit language; Jen and I are available Monday afternoon.

— Tom
Sr. Privacy Counsel, MapleHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Liu <tom.liu@maplehealth.com>, Jen Silver <jen.silver@maplehealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 May 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications: PII flows, subprocessors, and export scenarios

Tom / Jen —

Thanks for the review and concrete redlines. Quick answers and a proposed text snippet below. See also dpa_annex_redlines_20280513.docx (attached) for suggested legal language.

1) BackupPartner key custody
- BackupPartner stores encrypted snapshots only. Long-lived decryption keys are retained exclusively within our KMS; BackupPartner has no persistent key material. For Dedicated/private deployments we offer customer-managed keys (CMK) in the customer's KMS — Redwood never stores CMKs.

2) Tokenizer deterministic behavior
- Tokenization is salted by default (per-customer salt) so outputs are not globally deterministic. There is an opt-in deterministic mode for migration scenarios; this must be explicitly enabled and requires contractual acknowledgment in the annex.

3) Proposed contract language (suggestion)
- "Redwood will provide a current list of subprocessors and the specific processing roles that may access identifiers. Redwood will notify Customer at least 48 hours prior to onboarding any subprocessor that may have access to identifier-level logs or cleartext PII. Such notification will include the subprocessor's name, location, and the scope of access.
- For transient cross-border processing, Redwood will limit non-EU processing of EU-origin requests to a maximum of 6 hours in failover scenarios unless Customer explicitly consents to longer durations; extended processing for more than 24 hours will require written approval."

Action items
- Ive dropped the proposed text and our evidence files into the Drive.
- Aditya / Jonas: please confirm the 6-hour default window and whether ops can add an alerting/rollback mechanism.
- Jen / Tom: if that language looks workable, we can incorporate it into the DPA annex and share a final redline by Tuesday EOB.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference

Attachments: dpa_annex_redlines_20280513.docx
